declared: 2026-11-08, before the frozen rustc 1.98.0 oracle of these exact bytes and before any candidate run of these bytes. The shapes reduce census 10's crate record (core's `impl<F: FnPtr> PartialEq for F`, ptr/mod.rs:2592, "overlapping implementation headers have no specialization ordering"). Census batch 9 ran two related drafts (obj/parallel/census-batch9/repro/fnptr-tuple-spec.rs and fnptr-ref-spec.rs, a non-const `PartialEq` with a one-element tuple impl or core's `&A` impl, with `min_specialization` and without `with_negative_coherence`) through the census 10 pin and, for exploration, through rustc 1.98.0, which accepted the tuple draft and rejected the reference draft with E0119; `stable-tuple` and `stable-core-references` are the nearest of these controls, and no control here was run by anyone. Each outcome follows the rule read in the pinned rustc 1.98.0 sources (compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/traits/coherence.rs `overlap` and `impl_intersection_has_negative_obligation`, compiler/rustc_next_trait_solver/src/solve/trait_goals.rs `consider_builtin_fn_ptr_trait_candidate`, compiler/rustc_type_ir/src/ty_kind.rs `is_known_rigid`): in every mode, `T: FnPtr` holds only for a function pointer, so a knowable goal whose Self type is any other type constructor is impossible; without `with_negative_coherence` a goal whose Self type is a reference or a fundamental nominal over an unknown type is not knowable, because a downstream crate could own that Self type, and the impls overlap (E0119); with `with_negative_coherence`, as core enables at lib.rs:166, coherence also proves a negated where clause over the intersection with its unknowns as placeholders, and the builtin `impl !FnPtr for T` holds for every rigid type that is not a function pointer, so a reference, a fundamental nominal, a tuple or a trait object is disjoint from the blanket impl, while a placeholder parameter or a function pointer is not; a strict coherence trait keeps only that negative reasoning

core-references.rs.reason: core's exact shapes under core's features (`min_specialization`, `with_negative_coherence`): the const trait `PartialEq`, the blanket `impl<F: FnPtr> PartialEq for F` (ptr/mod.rs:2592) and core's four const reference impls `PartialEq<&B> for &A`, `PartialEq<&mut B> for &mut A`, `PartialEq<&mut B> for &A` and `PartialEq<&B> for &mut A` under `A: [const] PartialEq<B>` (cmp.rs:2117, 2192, 2265, 2281); `&A: !FnPtr` holds

reference.rs.reason: negative coherence: the blanket `impl<F: FnPtr> Mark for F` beside `impl<T: PointeeSized> Mark for &T`; `&T: !FnPtr` holds

fundamental.rs.reason: negative coherence: the blanket beside `impl<T> Mark for Wrap<T>` over a `#[fundamental]` struct; `Wrap<T>: !FnPtr` holds

trait-object.rs.reason: guard: negative coherence with the blanket beside `impl Mark for dyn Local`, core's `impl Debug for dyn Any` shape (any.rs:152); the trait object is neither sized nor a function pointer

parameter.rs.reason: opponent: negative coherence with the blanket beside `impl<T: Other> Mark for T`; the intersection's Self type is a placeholder, which is not rigid, so nothing is refuted and the impls overlap (E0119)

function-pointer.rs.reason: opponent: negative coherence with the blanket beside `impl Mark for fn()`; a function pointer implements `FnPtr`, so the impls overlap (E0119)

strict-tuple.rs.reason: a `#[rustc_strict_coherence]` trait: the blanket beside `impl<T> Mark for (T,)`; strict mode has no implicit absence, and the builtin `(T,): !FnPtr` still holds

stable-core-references.rs.reason: opponent: `core-references` without `with_negative_coherence`; `&_: FnPtr` is not knowable because a downstream crate could own `&Local`, so the impls overlap (E0119)

stable-fundamental.rs.reason: opponent: `fundamental` without `with_negative_coherence`; a downstream crate could own `Wrap<Local>` (E0119)

stable-tuple.rs.reason: stable coherence: the blanket beside `impl<T> Mark for (T,)`; a tuple is not fundamental, so `(_,): FnPtr` is knowable and impossible

stable-nominal.rs.reason: stable coherence: the blanket beside `impl<T> Mark for Holder<T>` over an ordinary generic struct

stable-raw-pointer.rs.reason: stable coherence: the blanket beside `impl<T: PointeeSized> Mark for *const T`

stable-array.rs.reason: stable coherence: the blanket beside `impl<T, const N: usize> Mark for [T; N]`
